clue.text: Asian cape's relocated in a body of water

indicators.note: things relocated are moved about, so the letters of these two words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A headland in Asia has been moved into a lake or sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocated' shuffles ASIANCAPES (the possessive 's supplies the final S) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's largest inland lake, between Europe and Asia, is a body of water.

clue.text: A couple of lines in atrocious poem

indicators.note: the word in tells us the first pieces sit inside the word for atrocious

parts.note: atrocious means very bad
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL

explanation.surface: A dreadful poem contains a couple of lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places A plus LL inside BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative song or verse in short stanzas is a kind of poem.

clue.text: Drips etc splashed according to plan

indicators.note: liquid splashed about lands in disorder, so the letters of these words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Paint drips and other marks were splashed on deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something following a written script happens as planned.

clue.text: Roman soldier one pictures returning with nothing

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the words for one and pictures are read backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
pics is short for pictures
the letter O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier comes home with his pictures and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns IPICS round to SCIPI, then O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who defeated Hannibal.

clue.text: Un-archaic English, possibly? Not this sort!

definitions.text: Un-archaic English, possibly? Not this sort!

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters before it

explanation.surface: A joke that modern English is anything but the medieval poet's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges UNARCHAIC plus E; the whole clue then defines: the poet's Middle English is precisely not un-archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of the Canterbury Tales poet is archaic Middle English, the opposite of un-archaic.

clue.text: Playwright who's all the rage?

parts.note: read as a dramatist full of fury rather than a fashionable one, it names the 1950s label for John Osborne and his generation

explanation.definitionFit: The label for John Osborne and fellow 1950s writers of angry, anti-establishment drama.

clue.text: Magic bees are associated with this

definitions.meaning: casting charms or enchantments is a form of magic
a bee is a competition, and a well-known kind tests how words are written

explanation.definitionFit: Casting charms is magic; a contest of writing words letter by letter is a famous kind of bee.

clue.text: Recipe providing filling for pale-coloured flan

indicators.note: the first word is placed inside the second, as filling goes inside a case

parts.note: pasty means pale and unhealthy-looking
R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin, take)

explanation.surface: A recipe gives the filling for a pale flan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing filling for' puts R inside PASTY; R for recipe comes from prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open tart made with a dough case, so it is a baked dough item.

clue.text: Someone liable to arrest and being kept in a small amount

indicators.note: the word and is held inside the word for a small amount

parts.note: a bit is a small amount

explanation.surface: Someone at risk of arrest keeps a little on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being kept in' puts AND inside BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw or robber is someone the police would arrest.

clue.text: Old soldiers redesigned one army yard

indicators.note: something redesigned is rebuilt in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Veterans have reorganised one army's parade ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical volunteer cavalry force of landowning farmers, so a body of former soldiers.

clue.text: Suez vendor disrupted meeting

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trader in Suez breaks up a planned meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A prearranged meeting at an agreed time and place.

clue.text: Be clear: seating not required for debate

parts.note: a stand at a venue is where spectators are on their feet, no seats needed
for can mean to, as in 'a present for her' or 'to her'
to reason is to argue or debate

explanation.surface: No chairs are needed for this discussion, it's obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom meaning to be obviously true.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is logically obvious, it is plain and evident.

indicators.note: the word in places the lecturer group inside the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled by' puts M inside DON, and 'in' puts that inside ETON, the English boarding school.

clue.text: Jail a girl pinching one from Commonwealth country

parts.note: can is slang for prison
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: A girl is locked up for pinching something in a Commonwealth country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' has the girl DI take AN for herself, placed after her.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from Canada, a Commonwealth member nation, is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Close friend losing a hint of timidity eventually

indicators.note: losing means the following letters are dropped from the friend's word

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend

indicators.note: a hint is a trace, so only the first letter of timidity is used

explanation.surface: A friend who sheds a little shyness given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes A and T (the first letter of timidity, from 'hint of') out of INTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means sooner or later, so given enough time.

clue.text: Stuff turkey initially carried by mother

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the letter goes within the word for mother

parts.note: mater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for mother

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of turkey

explanation.surface: Mum carries in the Christmas turkey stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives T, and 'carried by' puts it inside MATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical substance, the material things are made of.

clue.text: Unfinished article on people in ancient Aegean region

parts.note: the definite article
a race is a people or nation

clue.text: Energy? Tearaways reflected it

parts.note: a rip is a reckless, dissolute person, a tearaway

explanation.surface: Is energy what wild youngsters see in the mirror?
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit is liveliness and vigour.

clue.text: Move slowly left, entering capsule

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the letter goes within the capsule word

parts.note: a pod is a capsule, as in a space pod

explanation.surface: An astronaut moves sluggishly on climbing into the space capsule.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge along heavily is to move slowly.

clue.text: Tree feller seen with trees

parts.note: a feller is a man (informal 'fellow')
a grove is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: A lumberjack beside a stand of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like a woodcutter, but it is a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical coastal tree that grows in salt water.
